chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim al-Sha'iri and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding directing the deceased, you face his face towards the Qiblah and place his feet towards what follows the Qiblah.
ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be positioned in the grave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of orienting the deceased towards the Qiblah, a practice rooted in the belief that the dead continue to face their Lord in the grave. While some jurists debate whether this orientation is for the face or the side, this report explicitly mandates facing the Qiblah directly, reflecting the Shia emphasis on aligning the believer's final resting place with the direction of divine worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Al Shaeery and someone else,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding making the deceased to face by his face towads the Qiblah: ‘You should make his feet from what follows the Qiblah’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim al-Shu’ayriy and more than one person who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
facing a dying person toward Qiblah is turning his face in that direction such that the undersides of his feet point toward Qiblah.”
